channel.title: PC Workman — Build in Public Blog
channel.description: Three weekly series documenting the development of PC Workman, an AI-powered Windows system monitor: Monday Grind Blueprint, Wednesday Code Autopsy, Friday Shipped & Scarred. By Marcin Firmuga, HCK_Labs.

item.title: Is My PC Healthy? A Five-Minute Check
item.description: Five checks that separate a normally busy PC from a real problem, without reducing system health to one synthetic score.

item.title: Why Is My RAM Usage So High?
item.description: Available memory and page faults explain more than a percentage alone. Learn when Windows memory use is normal and when to act.

item.title: What Is This Process in Task Manager?
item.description: File path, digital signature, parent process and behavior are stronger evidence than a process name by itself.

item.title: Will This CPU Work With My Motherboard?
item.description: Socket is only the first compatibility layer. Check generation, chipset, BIOS support and power delivery before buying.

item.title: 6,533 Lines in One File: Breaking Up the Monolith Without Changing Its API
item.description: The hck_GPT response builder was split into eight mixins behind one facade. Two tests keep the files from growing back into a monolith.

item.title: From a Warehouse Floor to the Microsoft Store
item.description: A year ago I scanned barcodes and coded every night because I was afraid of disappearing. Today PC Workman — a Windows monitor with a fully offline AI — is on the Microsoft Store, permanently. The whole story, and the math underneath it.

item.title: Friday Shipped & Scarred #14: Microsoft Store Said No — Over a Blurry Icon and the Wrong Link
item.description: My first .msix, a full Partner Center submission, v1.8.0 stable — and a rejection over a blurry tile icon and a privacy link pointing at my security policy. A checklist, not a no.

item.title: Wednesday Code Autopsy #14: My AI Had a Brain — It Just Couldn't Reach It
item.description: Two tested learning engines the chat never called — a bare except: pass swallowed the NameError that wired them in, dead for four months and silent.

item.title: Monday Grind Blueprint #13: Every Gaming Tool Picks Your Overlay. Mine Starts Empty.
item.description: An in-game overlay that shows nothing until you choose, and greets you by the game you launched. v1.8.0 ships and the project turns one year old.

item.title: I Was Supposed to Fix Bugs. I Accidentally Built Two Features Instead. PC Workman 1.7.8
item.description: Thermal baseline learning and voltage SPC — the two features that grew out of a bug-fixing week. PC Workman 1.7.8.

item.title: I Built an AI-Powered PC Monitor in Python. 28 Strangers Shaped Its Brain. PC Workman 1.7.6
item.description: How 28 community members shaped hck_GPT's 82 intents. DeepMonitor, the 2.5D PC map and Wave 2 of the offline assistant.

item.title: Wednesday Code Autopsy #4: The Canvas Arc Nobody Uses — PC Workman
item.description: Tkinter's create_arc — the forgotten canvas primitive behind PC Workman's driver health gauge.

item.title: Monday Grind Blueprint #3: I Built a Driver Booster Competitor From Scratch — PC Workman v1.7.2
item.description: The week's plan: driver health scanning without the bloatware — what became First Setup & Drivers.

item.title: Friday Shipped & Scarred #3: PC Workman 1.7.1 — The Foundation Great Release
item.description: Stats Engine v2 shipped: the SQLite time-series pipeline every later feature stands on.

item.title: Monday Grind Blueprint #2: 80 Processes Explained, 3 Issues Targeted, 1 Week to Ship
item.description: Growing the process library and committing publicly to three community-reported issues in one week.

item.title: Friday Shipped & Scarred #1: The Day git --force Deleted 130 PC Workman Commits
item.description: The week the repo died on a Tuesday. Recovery via reflog — 90 of 130 commits back — and the backup rule born from it.

item.title: Code Autopsy #1: How ~90 Lines Turned System Monitoring Into A Conversation
item.description: The first intent parser — the ~90-line seed that grew into hck_GPT's 82 offline intents.
